the prediction of the three‐dimension structure of caspases.

the development of a novel approach that combines comparative sequence analysis and homology modeling to predict the tertiary structure of caspases, as well as to identify the key residues for substrate/inhibitor recognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
caspase family structures are not only converging, but are also diverging in a subtle way.
the caspase‐inhibitor complex model presented in the present paper is consistent with the available biochemical and structural data.

the predicted structure of casapase‐9 is consistent with available experimental data and can be used to guide further studies of caspase structure–function relationships and the design of caspase inhibitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the caspase‐family members are highly similar in the overall topology of their catalytic domains, but they differ substantially in the surface loops and the active site subsites.
the predicted tertiary structure of caspases is a reliable tool for understanding and manipulating the apoptotic machinery in health and disease.

, with a combination of experimental and modeling approaches, we have been able to provide a detailed picture of the structure–function relationship of the caspases, and in particular caspase‐6 and caspase ‐9, two of the most intriguing members of the family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the segment matching modeling procedure can be successfully used to predict the tertiary structures of caspase family enzymes and their interactions with inhibitors.
the segment‐matching modeling approach can provide a reliable prediction of the tertiary structure for a caspase family member for which no crystal structure is available.
the structure of the catalytically active site in caspase 9 is very similar to that found in caspase-8, but the overall fold of the two enzymes is very different.
